ID 27920431 | Container Port © Xuejingwen | Dreamstime.com
By Gavin van Marle
27 November 2026
Container spot freight rates on the Asia-Mediterranean trade were the only deepsea route prices that gained this week, as Transpacific and Asia-Europe rates further diverged.
According to this week’s World Container Index (WCI) by Drewry, its spot rate for Shanghai-Genoa saw an 8% week-on-week increase, to end at $4,802 per 40ft, while Shanghai-Rotterdam was unchanged for a second week. at $3,485 per 40ft.
Meanwhile, next week could see a renewed hike in Asia-Europe spot rates, with carriers clearly shaping up to push for higher short-term prices for December with a series of peak season surcharges (PSS) scheduled to be applied on 1 December.
Justified on the basis of an early Chinese New Year in 2027, both CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd have set a PSS of $1,000 per 40ft on Asia-North Europe shipments. Hapag-Lloyd also introducing a $1,500 per 40ft PSS on Asia-Mediterranean bookings on the same day.
These are expected to be supported by further surcharges and new FAK levels introduced by other carriers next month. Maersk has set a PSS of $1,500 per 40ft for Asia-North Europe and $2,000 per 40ft to the Mediterranean, both for implementation on 14 December.
On the same day, MSC will revise its FAK pricing on the two routes – rising from $4,600 to $5,600 per 40ft on Asia-North Europe, and a much more aggressive $7,500 per 40ft on Asia-Mediterranean shipments, currently $5,300 per 40ft, following its 15 November FAK notice.
Xeneta chief analyst Peter Sand said the price hikes were beginning to filter into the platform’s short-term rate outlook.
“Early Xeneta data indicates average spot rates to Mediterranean will increase a further 10% to 15% at the start of December, having already increased 27% since 14 October.
“An uptick is also expected into North Europe,” he added.
While next week’s rate increases are set to be accompanied by a higher degree of blanked sailings – Drewry’s Container Capacity Insight records seven – three Asia-North Europe and four Asia-Mediterranean – for next week, compared with four that took place this week, three Asia-North Europe and one Asia- Mediterranean.
The forecast December rate increases will coincide with predictions that capacity next month could be among the highest on record.
“Rates for the last week of November range from $2,700 to $3,200 per 40ft, against last week’s SCFI [Shanghai International Freight Index] assessment at $3,356 per 40ft, with capacity pressure building and December sailings expected to reach a new record high,” Linerlytica noted this week.
The analyst’s forward-looking capacity projections are for a monthly average of 400,000 teu capacity a week in December, up from around 350,000 teu a week this month.
According to Xeneta data, current capacity into North Europe is 4.9% higher than a month ago, and up 6.7% to the Mediterranean.
With yesterday’s Thanksgiving holiday bringing a quiet week on the Transpacific trade, rates on the WCI’s Shanghai-Los Angeles route fell 8% week on week, to end at $6,437 per 40ft, while its Shanghai-New York leg was down 7%, to $7,615 per 40ft.
“The upward trend into Europe contrasts with fronthauls into the US, where early Xeneta data indicates further spot rate declines at the start of December,” Mr Sand said. “Average spot rates have already fallen 12% into US east coast and 7.6% into US west coast since 14 October.
“The most recent Xeneta data paints a rosier picture for US shippers, but a wider market perspective changes the situation dramatically: despite the softening in October and November, average spot rates to US west coast remain up 310%, compared with pre-Hormuz crisis levels on 28 February. Into the US east coast, average spot rates are up 283%.
“From the Far East to Mediterranean and North Europe, the recent increases mean average spot rates are up a much smaller 54% and 53% respectively, compared with pre-Hormuz crisis levels,” he added.
